page: Microsoft Azure F2amds_v7 is a memory-intensive virtual machine instance powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this server features 2 virtual CPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. The hardware configuration includes a bundled 236 GB NVMe SSD for local storage and supports premium storage options.

Benchmark data highlights exceptional single-core capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier performance in stress-ng single-core CPU tests, Geekbench single-core scoring, and single-threaded text processing. Cryptographic and compression workloads also perform well, with gzip compression and bzip3 decompression single-threaded operations reaching top-tier throughput. However, multi-threaded scaling is more limited due to the 2-core constraint, resulting in average multi-core CPU performance and weak multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth and database operations score in the average tier, while Redis SET operations and static web serving throughput fall into the weaker performance category.

The F2amds_v7 offers a cost-efficient profile for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallelization. The high memory allocation per core makes it suitable for small-scale database operations, memory-cached applications, and single-threaded data processing tasks. However, the low core count limits its suitability for heavy multi-threaded compiling, ray tracing, or medium-to-large language model inference, where prompt processing speeds drop significantly.
